sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke. 2020. On the genetic position of Chakpa within Luish languages. Himalayan Linguistics 19(2) [Languages and Peoples of the Eastern Himalayan Region]: 44-55. doi:10.5070/H91150999.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2.2.4 'Tones', p.49: 'Generally speaking, tones of Chakpa are unknown as they are no longer spoken nor recorded. Ch. Y. Singh (2014) shows two distinctive tones (mid and high) for Chakpa. However, compared with Cak, Kadu, and Ganan, the correspondence is irregular.' p.45: McCulloch 1859 'is the best material published so far'; Huziwara 2013b = 「アンドロ語文法の再構」 (A reconstruction of Andro grammar), paper at 日本歴史言語学会第3回大会 -- a conference paper, not a KULR article.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page andr1246 'Andro' and reference records 51830 (McCulloch 1859), 587674 (Huziwara 2020), 587676 (Huziwara 2019 Phayeng handout).
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Andro = Sak (Luish), extinct (Moseley 2010), 'documented by a wordlist in McCulloch 1859'; other refs are classificatory (DeLancey 2015, van Driem 2001, Matisoff 2012, Huziwara 2020 listed by Glottolog as a comparative study) and the unshareable Phayeng handout (Huziwara 2019, listed by Glottolog as a phonology;comparative, nosharefn). No grammar or phonology of Andro is listed.

sources.citation: 藤原敬介 [Huziwara, Keisuke]. 2014. ルイ祖語の再考 [Proto-Luish reconsidered]. 京都大学言語学研究 33: 1-32. hdl:2433/196280.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2.1 p.2: 'アンドロ語（Andro: A）：McCulloch［1859］による。声調は記録されていない。' (Andro: from McCulloch 1859; tones not recorded). Note 5 cites Huziwara 2013b for the suggestion that McCulloch's {u}/{a} spellings may encode a vowel-length contrast.

sources.citation: 藤原敬介 [Huziwara, Keisuke]. 2012. ルイ祖語の再構にむけて [Toward a reconstruction of Proto-Luish]. 京都大学言語学研究 [Kyoto University Linguistic Research] 31: 25-131. hdl:2433/182194, doi:10.14989/182194.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 2.1 p.31: '●Andro (A): McCulloch [1859] による。声調は記録されていない。' (Andro data are from McCulloch 1859; tones are not recorded). Sec. 8.3 p.124: 'A/Se については声調が記録されていないので対応がわからない' (for Andro/Sengmai tone correspondences cannot be known because tones were not recorded). Proto-Luish tones (H vs L) reconstructed from Cak/Kadu/Ganan only.

sources.citation: McCulloch, W. 1859. Account of the Valley of Munnipore and of the Hill Tribes; with a Comparative Vocabulary of the Munnipore and other languages. Selections from the Records of the Government of India (Foreign Department) 27. Calcutta: Bengal Printing Co. Appendix: Comparative Vocabulary (Undro and Sengmai column).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only primary data on Andro: c. 423 words and some sentences in an 'Undro and Sengmai' column. The preface (Appendix p.i) gives only a spelling key ('a is pronounced as in Italian.. th always has the h aspirated'); no mention or marking of stress, accent or tone (the occasional acute, e.g. Toorel, Sen, is a vowel-quality mark per the key).

sources.citation: 藤原敬介 [Huziwara, Keisuke]. 2019. 「パイェン語の言語特徴」 [Phayeng language features]. Handout (23 pp.), 日本歴史言語学会第9回大会, Hiroshima University, 2019-12-15. Glottolog ref 587676 (listed by Glottolog as a phonology;comparative, nosharefn).

sources.citation: Singh, Ch. Yashawanta. 2014. A linguistic study of dead language -- Chakpa. Paper presented at SEALS 24, Yangon University, Yangon.

sources.note: Only modern first-hand description of Chakpa (Andro) from fieldwork with ritual reciters; Huziwara 2020 p.49 reports it posits two tones (mid, high); if any prosodic (stress or tone) statement on Andro exists, it is here.
